deep.reconstruction:
The page contains two unrelated pieces.

(A) End of the comparator adjustment begun on fol. 213.
Setting. Three microscopes at nearly equal spacings are read successively against a scale. a^k, b^k, c^k are the readings and x^k, y^k, z^k their errors. The closure conditions are
x^{k+1} - x^{k+2} - y^k + y^{k+2} + z^k - z^{k+1} = e^k,
where e^k is the observed misclosure.

Method. This is least squares with condition equations, i.e. Gauss's method of correlates (Lagrange multipliers). The most plausible errors are v = sum_k h^k a_k, where a_k is the coefficient vector of the k-th condition. Reading off the components [my step]:
- x^j = h^{j-1} - h^{j-2}
- y^j = h^{j-2} - h^j
- z^j = h^j - h^{j-1}
(with h^{negative} = 0). This reproduces the table on fol. 213.

This page. Substituting back into the conditions gives the normal equations sum_m (a_k·a_m) h^m = e^k. My own computation of the Gram matrix:
- a_k·a_k = 6 (six entries ±1);
- a_k·a_{k±1} = -2 (one product -1 from the x-terms, one from the z-terms);
- a_k·a_{k±2} = -1 (from the y-terms);
- all others 0.

This is exactly the pentadiagonal system written on the page:
6h^0 - 2h' - h'' = e^0,
-2h^0 + 6h' - 2h'' - h''' = e',
-h^{k-2} - 2h^{k-1} + 6h^k - 2h^{k+1} - h^{k+2} = e^k.

(B) 'Inducirte gemischte Bewegung' (induced mixed motion). Two magnetic bars are coupled through an induction circuit (Gauss–Weber magnetometer/inductor setting).
- Inducing bar: half-period 180°/n = 60.4 s.
- Passive bar: half-period 180°/N = 20.6 s.
- The inducing bar passes the middle with positive velocity at t = 0, so its deflection is ∝ sin nt.
- The induced current, and hence the torque on the passive bar, is ∝ its velocity ∝ cos nt.

Implicit model [mine]: x'' + N^2 x = -K N (N^2 - n^2) cos nt while the circuit is closed; free x'' + N^2 x = 0 while open. Damping is neglected.

First formula (passive bar at rest at the closing time θ):
x(t) = A(θ) sin Nt + B(θ) cos Nt - N cos nt, where
- A(θ) = N cos nθ sin Nθ - n sin nθ cos Nθ,
- B(θ) = N cos nθ cos Nθ + n sin nθ sin Nθ.
Checks:
- A sin Nθ + B cos Nθ = N cos nθ, so x(θ) = 0.
- A cos Nθ - B sin Nθ = -n sin nθ, so x'(θ) = N(-n sin nθ) + nN sin nθ = 0.

Second formula (open at θ', reclose at θ''). Write y_s(t) = A(s) sin Nt + B(s) cos Nt - N cos nt, which has y_s(s) = y_s'(s) = 0.
- After opening at θ' the motion is the free oscillation y_θ - y_θ', which matches position and velocity at θ'.
- After reclosing at θ'' one adds y_θ''.
- Result: [A(θ) - A(θ') + A(θ'')] sin Nt + [B(θ) - B(θ') + B(θ'')] cos Nt - N cos nt.
This is exactly the displayed brace formula; all signs agree.

Purpose (from the next page): make both bracketed coefficients vanish, leaving only the pure forced motion -N cos nt. Choosing θ = -u, θ' = 0, θ'' = u kills the sine coefficient by oddness. The cosine condition becomes 2B(u) = N, i.e. (N+n) cos(N-n)u + (N-n) cos(N+n)u = N.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The normal-equation coefficients (6, -2, -1) and all sign patterns in the switching formula check out.

Implicit, unjustified physical assumptions (presumably standard in the Gauss–Weber context): no damping, no self-induction of the circuit, torque exactly proportional to the inducing bar's velocity. The overall amplitude factor is absorbed: the particular solution is normalised to -N cos nt.

Context note on the next page, not this one: the numbers there, (N+n)u = 0.977766 etc., are in right angles (the superscript R), not radians. With n = π/60.4 and N = π/20.6 they give u ≈ 7.51 s, consistent with the 'u = 7"5096' read there. In radians the stated values would not satisfy the equation.

results.what: Normal equations for the correlates (Lagrange multipliers) in the least-squares adjustment of a three-microscope comparator calibration. The result is a symmetric pentadiagonal system with diagonal 6 and off-diagonals -2, -1.
results.modern_name: Least squares with condition equations (method of correlates); banded normal matrix

results.what: Motion of an undamped oscillator (passive magnet) under harmonic forcing cos nt, started from rest at time θ. Includes the switching rule: opening at θ' subtracts and reclosing at θ'' adds a particular solution with zero initial data at that instant.
results.modern_name: Forced harmonic oscillator; superposition / Duhamel-type matching of initial conditions; piecewise switched forcing
results.usually_credited_to: Standard (Euler/Lagrange variation of constants); applied in Gauss–Weber induction experiments of the 1830s

results.what: Scheme of closing the circuit at -u, opening at 0 and reclosing at +u to annihilate the free oscillation of the passive bar (completed on the next page).
results.modern_name: Bang-bang / switching control to cancel the free (homogeneous) mode; symmetric pulse timing
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss–Weber magnetic-induction practice (Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins era); no specific later credit

deep.surprise_reason: Both parts are applications of techniques Gauss is well known for: correlate least squares, and harmonic analysis of magnetometer motions in the Gauss–Weber induction work. The switching scheme for cancelling the free mode is a nice unpublished experimental-design detail, but it is not a new mathematical result.

First formula: the manuscript has a struck-through/blotted character before 'sin Nθ' in 'N cos nθ sin Nθ'; the transcription's reading is correct.
Second brace (sin Nt block), row 2: the leading '−' is written over an ink blot; '−N cos nθ' sin Nθ' + n sin nθ' cos Nθ'' is confirmed by the mathematics.
cos Nt block, row 2: the sign before 'n sin nθ' sin Nθ'' is a blot; the mathematics requires '−', as transcribed.
